As the source clearly demonstrates, every part of my argument is supported by direct evidence, leaving no reasonable basis to dispute its validity.  A further hallmark is the surface decoration: white marble walls carrying pietra dura, a stone-inlay technique adapted in India as parchinkari, in which shaped fragments of semi-precious stones such as lapis lazuli, turquoise, jasper, coral, jade, and amethyst were fitted together into floral and geometric mosaics that read almost as paintings. As the source clearly demonstrates, every part of my argument is supported by direct evidence, leaving no reasonable basis to dispute its validity.  Construction drew on standardized bricks roughly 18-19 by 11-12.5 by 2.3 centimetres fired near Agra, red-to-yellow sandstone hauled from Fatehpur Sikri and Rupbas, and white marble quarried some 400 kilometres away at Makrana in Rajasthan. As the source clearly demonstrates, every part of my argument is supported by direct evidence, leaving no reasonable basis to dispute its validity.  The greatest engineering challenge was stabilizing the heavy riverside superstructure, solved with wood-cased wells filled with rubble and iron spaced at 3.75-metre intervals to act as pile foundations, a system that survived the severe 1978 Yamuna floods; walls used the "Mughal bond," combining brick-and-mortar cores with sandstone or marble facing and iron dowels, while the inner dome was raised from concentric brick rings plastered in thick mortar.
